::: notes
Welcome. We have two halves with a break between them, and one published claim to work on throughout. In the first half I give you the vocabulary of reproduction, robustness and replication, then the case: an experiment in which a thousand emails asked housing authorities in the United States how to apply for public housing, and the finding that replies to some names were less likely to greet the sender by name. We work out what question that claim answers, and you reproduce a result that one of five independent analysts reported for it. In the second half you vary the analysis yourself, we read what the class produced, and we finish with the new study that tested the claim on new data.
:::
